correctness.rationale: For k>=2,n>=4k+1, the first counting-refinement round separates root, the union T_1..T_k, and the far tail. The round-two near-to-far counts are j for 1<=j<=k and far-to-near counts 2k-j+1 for k<j<=2k. Each later tail index a<j<=a+k has first separated neighbor T_{j-k}, while more distant tail points have none; reflection enforces no within-T_j separation. The last residual distance alone is a class, so strict first stabilization is ceil((floor(n/2)-1)/k). At n=4k the antipodal wraparound makes T_{2k-1},T_{2k} coalesce at round two and split at round three using T_{k-1}. The argument covers all integers in the stated domain, independently corroborated by new direct exact refinement for 265 pairs and 10 boundary cases; finite checks do not prove the induction.
residual_risks: No claim for 2k+2<=n<4k; 1-WL exact rooted object only, not graph canonization or arbitrary circulants.
